title: Close-range grass control
opening: Vine Whip strikes an arc. Keep an open edge of the crowd in front of you and use later range upgrades instead of walking into its center.
planning: Grass / Poison opens both attack families alongside Normal. Power supports the opening evolution; Reflexes supports Razor Leaf. Pick coverage that you can switch to when it is needed.

title: A straightforward projectile start
opening: Ember targets the nearest enemy. Work toward its move levels and take Power during the same run while focusing on a safe movement route.
planning: Fire Spin supplies orbit coverage while active; Flame Wheel rewards letting enemies follow your trail. Separate move slots do not all fire together.

title: Fire attacks with flying coverage
opening: Charizard also begins with Ember but has its own attack multiplier, speed and Flying pool. Use its movement to keep space for projectile or orbit attacks.
planning: Power supports Ember and Wing Attack; Synthesis supports Fire Spin. Terrain movement is decided by the sprite’s hovering flag, not the Flying type alone.

title: Line up the water stream
opening: Water Gun is a piercing projectile. Circle so enemies line up along a clear firing route instead of crossing a packed group for experience.
planning: Power supports Water Gun and Hydro Pump; Sprint supports Bubble. Choose a second attack to solve a visible problem rather than splitting levels equally across every move.

title: Electric coverage with room to move
opening: Thunder Shock gives Pikachu a projectile opening. Its movement speed helps reposition, but does not protect you from staying in ground warnings.
planning: Power, Reflexes and Armor support these three Electric evolution paths. Secure one evolution first, then build the second path around the choices actually offered.

title: A Psychic opening in a Water pool
opening: Psyduck explicitly starts with Confusion despite its Water typing. The move can be upgraded, but this exception does not add the whole Psychic family to its normal level-up pool.
planning: Confusion uses Reflexes, Water Gun uses Power and Bubble uses Sprint. The game distinguishes the opening exception from the Normal + Water card pool.

title: Ghost and Poison pressure
opening: Gengar begins with Shadow Ball and has a strong base attack multiplier. Keep a clear projectile lane before committing to an experience pickup.
planning: Shadow Ball uses Reflexes, Hex uses Magnet and Sludge uses Power. These are source-compatible options, not measured best-in-slot claims.

title: Practice arcs, dashes and decoys
opening: Eevee begins with Tackle, making close-range arcs easy to observe. The Normal pool still includes several different attack behaviors.
planning: Vigor, Sprint and Armor unlock these three goals. A dash or decoy changes positioning; read its upgrade effect instead of comparing only raw damage.

title: Psychic and Fairy alternatives
opening: Gardevoir begins with Confusion and draws from Normal, Psychic and Fairy. Keep a primary evolution goal and choose another behavior for a clear weakness in your run.
planning: Confusion uses Reflexes, Psybeam uses Power and Dazzling Gleam uses Synthesis. Attack factor still combines with cooldown, coverage and enemy typing.

title: Melee timing with a ranged option
opening: Lucario opens with Karate Chop. Leave a way out of each close-range arc, and consider its Fighting / Steel ranged options when you need more distance.
planning: Power supports Karate Chop and Metal Claw; Reflexes supports Aura Sphere. One stat card can meet several compatible requirements, but each move needs its own level 5 and gold card.
